title: Certify GNOME and KDE Settings enrollment and PAM opt-in
summary: Certification of the GNOME (GTK4/libadwaita) enrollment wizard and the KDE (Plasma 6 KCM) settings module for end-to-end enrollment + PAM opt-in. CI cannot run clean GNOME or Plasma sessions, so the CI-testable surface is structural (binaries/modules staged, system-bus usage, install-manifest ownership, accessibility anchors, warning constants, PAM sufficient control, polkit policy) plus the existing unit-test suites in namtor-gnome (29 presenter + 12 privacy) and namtor-kde (18 lib + 3 abi-smoke). Real enrollment with a camera, real PAM toggle against /etc/pam.d, and real authentication against a running PAM stack are human-gated on a desktop VM and recorded below as WITHHELD.

structural: GNOME enroll-wizard binary staged (install-manifest package=gnome, target/release/namtor-enroll-wizard present)
KDE QML module files staged (main.qml, metadata.json, CMakeLists.txt install rules, libnamtorqml.so build artifact, libnamtor_kde.so Rust cdylib)
KDE desktop-integration files owned by package=kde in install-manifest (3 entries: .desktop, .metainfo.xml, .svg)
Both UIs use the SYSTEM bus: 0 Connection::session/sessionBus references across dbus_client.rs, bridge.rs, namtor_kcm.cpp; systemBus references present in all three

PAM sufficient control: pam-install.sh defaults CONTROL=sufficient; namtor-pam-config editor defaults to NamtorControl::Sufficient; pam_namtor maps all errors to PAM_AUTHINFO_UNAVAIL (fall-through to password)
Polkit action org.namtor.configure-pam declared in org.namtor.policy

gnome.pam_switch_tooltip: tooltip_text + set_tooltip_text on PAM service Switch (components/pam_services.rs)

no_tpm_warning.gnome: ProtectionView.is_software_fallback boolean drives 'Software fallback in use — templates are not hardware-bound.' warning banner in wizard.rs
no_tpm_warning.kde: protectionHasTpm Q_PROPERTY drives 'No TPM2 device — software fallback.' label in main.qml

gnome.text: FAR/FRR and real-attack PAD gates remain unmeasured. Enabling face authentication is experimental and not recommended for security-sensitive use.

kde.text: FAR/FRR and real-attack PAD gates remain unmeasured. Enabling face authentication is experimental and not recommended for security-sensitive use.
kde.qml_binding: pamConfirmDialog bound to highImpactWarning in main.qml

password_fallback.module_error_mapping: PAM_AUTHINFO_UNAVAIL on any daemon/timeout/error → sufficient → ignore → fall through to password module
password_fallback.rhost_refusal: PAM_RHOST set → refuse (spec §8.2); sshd classified Unsupported

withheld_human_gated.rationale: Clean GNOME and Plasma sessions cannot be run in CI. The following require a human-gated desktop VM with a real camera, real /etc/pam.d, and a running PAM stack.
scenarios: Real enrollment with a live IR camera (Discover settings surface → enroll → capture frames → review → commit → profile appears in list)
Real PAM service toggle against /etc/pam.d (list detected services → enable login → verify pam_namtor.so block inserted → disable → verify removed)
Real authentication against a running PAM stack (login/sudo/su/polkit with pam_namtor.so enabled → face match → success; daemon down → password fallback)
High-impact confirmation dialog rendered on a real display for login/sudo/su/polkit services
Accessibility verification with a real screen reader (Orca on GNOME, KMag/KRunner on KDE) and keyboard-only navigation
Persistence across session restart and reboot
Polkit prompt rendered on a real desktop for org.namtor.configure-pam

files_not_modified: No Rust source, Cargo.toml, distro packaging, install-manifest.toml, model-manifest.toml, or existing test scripts were modified.
